title: Modern Romance
author: Aziz Ansari with Eric Klinenberg
target_audience: Young adults and millennials navigating dating
Singles interested in online dating and modern relationships
Anyone curious about how technology shapes romance
Readers seeking a research-based yet entertaining look at dating
core_themes: Impact of technology (texting, social media, apps) on dating and romance
Changing expectations and norms in romantic relationships
Cross-cultural perspectives on love and courtship
Challenges and anxieties of modern courtship
primary_purpose: To explore how dating and romantic relationships have been transformed by technology and cultural shifts, combining social science research with humorous commentary to give readers deeper insight into the complexities of modern love.

structure_format.organization: Chapters structured thematically, each exploring different aspects of romance in the digital age
features: Anecdotes from real people and Ansari’s standup experiences
Results from interviews, focus groups, and original research
International case studies (e.g., Tokyo, Buenos Aires, Doha)

key_concepts_lessons: Dating choices have dramatically expanded, leading to both more opportunities and increased decision fatigue.
Texting and digital communication can create anxiety and misinterpretations.
Online dating platforms have changed how people meet and evaluate potential partners.
Romantic expectations have evolved—people are now seeking soulmates and personal fulfillment, not just companionship.
Cultural contexts still shape how people date and form relationships, even in a hyper-connected world.
The search for 'the perfect partner' can sometimes make forming real connections harder.
notable_features: Blend of comedic voice with rigorous research
Collaboration between a comedian and a sociologist
Use of real-world data and international comparisons
cultural_historical_context: Published in the mid-2010s, the book reflects a period of rapid technological change, with smartphones, dating apps, and social media dramatically reshaping the landscape of romance, courtship, and communication. It captures the zeitgeist and anxieties of millennials in their quest for meaningful connections.
reception_impact: Became a New York Times bestseller
Praised for balancing humor with insightful analysis
Well received for its original research and relatable observations
Critics highlighted it as more substantive than the average celebrity book
Popular among readers seeking both entertainment and sociological insight into dating
comparable_titles: All the Single Ladies by Rebecca Traister
The Science of Happily Ever After by Ty Tashiro
Attached by Amir Levine and Rachel Heller
